knowledge_point.title: Identifying the Leading Entries of a Matrix

question.:question/problem:
What is the sum of the leading entries of the $2$nd, $3$rd, and $4$th rows in the matrix $A$, given below?
$$
A = \begin{bmatrix}2 & 4 & 6 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -2\end{bmatrix}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The first non-zero entry of each row (from left to right) is the leading entry. 

Therefore, the leading entries of the $2\text{nd},$ $3\text{rd},$ and $4\text{th}$ rows of $A$ are $3,$ $1,$ and $2$, respectively.

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 4 & 6 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -2\end{bmatrix}
$$

So, the answer is $3+1+2=6.$
